editorial:
Imagine a world where the help actually runs the house, and that is exactly what you get here. You will meet Anthony, a valet who is completely fed up with his boss, the Count. While the Count is busy being a mess, Anthony spends his time grumbling under his breath and quietly fixing every mistake his employer makes. It is a funny look at a backwards relationship where the servant is clearly the smartest person in the room. The vibe is light and breezy, making it a perfect choice for when you just want to relax and laugh at some old-school chaos.

The acting is the best part, especially the way Anthony uses his facial expressions to show how much he dislikes his job. The pacing moves quickly, though some of the jokes feel a bit dated since it is from 1939. If you enjoy seeing a grumpy character win in the end, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the final act, Anthony's secret plan to save the estate finally pays off. He manages to trick the Count into making a smart financial move that prevents the family from losing everything. The Count thinks he did it all himself, but the other servants know the truth. It ends with Anthony still grumbling and complaining, but he is secretly happy knowing he is the real power behind the throne.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves witty banter and grumpy characters.
